name: Governance decisions
description: The corporate decision layer for any exercise: board briefings, a materiality worksheet, Form 8-K disclosure drafts, a business impact analysis, a ransom decision paper, legal hold and privilege notices, regulator inquiries, insurer and auditor notices, investor questions, a decision log and succession documents. Stays at the level of governance decisions and their records; it is an exercise aid, not legal advice, and every company, person and adviser in it is fictional.

glossary.definition: Information is material if there is a substantial likelihood a reasonable shareholder would consider it important, or that it would significantly alter the total mix of information. Quantitative and qualitative factors both count.

Report of a material cybersecurity incident: nature, scope and timing, and the material impact or reasonably likely material impact. Due four business days after the company determines the incident is material.
Other events. An incident not yet judged material may be reported here; the text does not claim materiality.
The Attorney General may delay disclosure for national security or public safety; asking for a delay does not change the duty, and the four business days run from the end of the delay.
Business impact analysis; recovery time objective (how soon a function must be back); recovery point objective (how much data loss is tolerable).
A hold tells people to preserve documents. Work done at counsel's direction is more likely to stay privileged; conclusions about fault do not belong in chat or email.

productConventions: Every document carries the line 'Exercise aid, not legal advice. Check the current rule and your counsel.'
Name the company as fictional; show no stock ticker and no real company name.
A decision record states who decided, when, what was known at that time and the basis.
Item 1.05 drafts state nature, scope, timing and material impact; Item 8.01 drafts do not claim materiality.
Dates and times are written out with the time zone when the clock matters.
realismRules: The materiality determination follows discovery without unreasonable delay; it cannot be put off by delaying a meeting.
The investigation need not finish before the determination; facts arrive late and change.
Paying or refusing a ransom does not remove the duty to decide on materiality.
The board, filing, press release and employee message must agree on the facts.
A recovery claim is checked against the RTO and elapsed time, not against the plan's hope.

criticalTasks: The crisis team, disclosure committee and board have clear roles and a call tree that reaches them
Legal, finance, security and continuity work from one set of facts
Outside counsel directs the forensic work so it stays privileged
Recovery order follows the business impact analysis and its dependencies
The continuity plan is activated at the right scope
Delegations of authority are known and current
The filing, press statement, employee message and investor answers agree
Statements say what is known, what is not and what is being done
No statement claims more than the facts support
The board hears what it needs, when it needs it
Regulators, the insurer and the auditor are told on their own clocks
A materiality determination is made without unreasonable delay and recorded with its basis
Facts that change are updated and earlier statements corrected
The investigation continues after the determination
The financial impact range is kept current and informs the materiality call
Functions are restored within their recovery time objectives, or the miss is recorded and explained
